title: Do an insulin pen's 2-unit safety shot with the needle up, then dial a 12-unit dose by its window
instruction: Get the insulin pen ready for a 12-unit dose: take off the needle shield and put it in its tray; do the 2-unit safety shot: needle up, push the dose knob in until it stops and hold it there 5 s so a drop shows at the needle tip; then set 12 units by the dose window and leave the pen in its tray.
context: Registered and licensed practical nurses in nursing homes and hospitals, and medical assistants in clinics that give insulin, give it from pens several times a day. The pen's instructions for use (Lilly, Humalog KwikPen IFU, https://uspl.lilly.com/humalog/humalog.html#section-18) start every injection the same way: pull off the outer and inner needle shields; turn the dose knob to 2 units; hold the pen with the needle pointing up; push the dose knob in until it stops and 0 shows in the dose window, hold it in while counting to 5 slowly, and "You should see insulin at the tip of the Needle" (if not, repeat, no more than 4 times). Then the dose is dialled by the window, not by counting clicks, and corrected by turning the knob either way. The knob clicks once a unit and screws out as it is dialled; the window shows even numbers and a line for each odd one.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of the table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A fluid-filled training pen of the KwikPen kind (0 to 60 units, 1 unit a click; its cartridge holds water), 166 mm long with a 4 mm pen needle screwed on and its outer needle shield on (the inner shield already off), 17 mm across the body, its dose knob 18 mm across, about 20 g, lies in a white plastic pen tray (50 x 210 mm, 3 mm rails) centred at (24, 12), along y, needle toward -y, its dose window facing down. The counter reads 0. An empty blue plastic shield tray (70 x 70 mm, 16 mm walls) is at (30, -11). Both trays are fixed to the table.
scoring: Video of the window and the needle, then a photo. 0.2: the shield off and in its tray at the end. +0.4: the safety shot, the shield off the needle (its middle 3 cm or more from the tip): the counter dialled to exactly 2, then pushed to 0 against the pen's 9.2 N, the needle within 30 degrees of straight up through the push and the hold, a drop at the needle tip, the knob held home 5 s (a push: a fingertip under the knob's end face moving it in; the window counts down with it). +0.4: after the shot, the counter at exactly 12 at the end, the pen lying in its tray, every fingertip of both hands more than 5 cm from the pen along its length. The 2 s hold gates only the full 1.0: every part met scores 0.6 until held 2 s; lower totals count at once. Caps: a push delivering units with the needle below horizontal: at most 0.2; the needle touching a finger or the table once the shield is off: at most 0.5; the pen dropped outside its tray: 0. A real trial uses a fluid-filled training pen and reads on video the window at 2, the needle's angle, the drop at the needle tip (a close camera on the needle) and the 5 s hold, then the window at 12 before the pen is laid down; no drop, no dose credited; a photo shows both trays.
reset_notes: The dose knob turned back to 0 without pushing (nothing delivered), a fresh pen needle with its outer shield on and its inner shield off, the needle tip wiped dry, the training pen's cartridge refilled with water when low, the pen in its tray as at the start; the shield tray empty. No seed changes the scene.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz on GPU. The knob's clicks (18 degrees a unit), its rise (0.33 mm a unit) and the count are a coupling in code, to be measured on a pen. The push meets a constant 9.2 N, a KwikPen's plateau injection force at 6 U/s (van der Burg 2011). The drop is shown at the needle tip once 2 units are pushed out with the needle up and the shield off; no liquid is simulated. The shield is held in code until a pinch draws it 3 mm. The needle has no collider.
